entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Sp Chadar- Govt. Advocate for the respondent-State
Heard on admission.
Trial Court record perused.
Prima facie, this appeal seems to be arguable.
Hence, admitted for final hearing.
Further heard on I.A. No.15491 of 2025, which is a first application under Section 430 of BNSS/389(1) of the CrPC, 1973 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 23.06.2025 passed by the learned Sessions Judge,
Dindori (M.P.) in ST No.85/2023, whereby the appellant has been convicted under Sections 376(1)
of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.5,000/- with default stipulations.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case, though the DNA report is negative in respect of present appellant.

As far as the statements of the prosecutrix and her husband are concerned, though they have supported the story of the prosecution in chief examination, but in cross-examination it is revealed that there was a previous enmity between the 2 CRA-6215-2025 husband of the prosecutrix and the present appellant in respect of appointment of maid.
The present appellant was appointed as maid while husband of the prosecutrix tried to appoint some other person of his choice as maid.
It is also admitted by the prosecutrix in para 4 and 5 that she and present appellant remained friends and when present appellant had caught her from the backside, she has not opposed him.
In view of the contradictions and variations in the statement of the prosecutrix, the appellant has a good case on merits.
The present appeal will take considerable time for its disposal.
The appellant is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.

Looking to the period of custody,
benefit of suspension of sentence may be granted and the appellant may be released on bail during pendency of this appeal.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer made by the appellant.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.

Keeping in view of the various facts reveal from the cross-examination of the prosecutrix as well as negative DNA report, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I.A. No.15491 of 2025 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail.

The present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial 3 CRA-6215-2025 Court on 03.08.2026 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
